We dream of a small, calm wedding in the Himalaya mountains, in one of the most sacred places in all of India. This page is our way to show you that place: how beautiful it is, why it is so special, and how we will travel there together, in comfort and care.

The story of this place

A wedding older than time

Long, long ago, the great God Shiva married the Goddess Parvati. People believe their wedding happened right here, at Triyuginarayan. A holy fire was lit for that divine wedding.

That same fire still burns today. It has never gone out. People call it the Akhand Dhuni, “the fire that never dies.”

When you marry here, you take your vows beside the very fire that saw the Gods marry.

Around the temple are four holy water pools, Rudra, Vishnu, Brahma and Saraswati Kund. Couples bathe in them to become pure before the wedding. The name Triyuginarayan means the temple has stood through three great ages of time. Many families believe a marriage blessed here is blessed forever.

Here, couples take their vows beside a fire that has never gone out.

The place around it

A place you will never forget

Triyuginarayan sits high in the green Garhwal Himalayas. Snow peaks stand all around. Mornings are misty, the air is clean, and the nights are full of stars. Nearby is Deoria Tal, a quiet lake that holds the giant snow mountains in its mirror. This is a place of peace, and a place of memories.

Deoria Tal, the lake that holds the mountains in its mirror.

The ceremony

How the wedding happens

It is small and peaceful, about 50 guests. Simple, holy, and beautiful.

1

Holy bath

The couple bathes in the sacred water pools to become pure.

2

The eternal fire

They sit beside the fire that has burned since the Gods’ wedding.

3

Seven rounds

The couple walks around the holy fire seven times together.

4

Blessing

The temple priest says the prayers and blesses the marriage.

How your wedding will look

Soft, simple, and full of nature

Not heavy. Not loud. The mountains are the decoration. Gentle flowers, warm light, calm colours, and the great Himalayas behind you. These are real weddings by the teams whose style we love.

A real wedding, at this very temple.

The journey from Guwahati

Easy, comfortable, and cared for

Two simple ways to reach the mountains. We arrange every part, with restful stops and plenty of breaks.

Option 1. Guwahati to Dehradun, then to the wedding
Guwahati→Delhi (change flights)→Dehradun (by air)→Rest night, Rishikesh→Drive up, with breaks→Triyuginarayan Temple

One flight with a single, easy change at Delhi. Then a calm drive to the venue.

Option 2. Guwahati to Delhi, then to the wedding
Guwahati→Delhi (stay the night)→Rishikesh or Haridwar (train or car)→Rest stops on the drive→Triyuginarayan Temple

Break the journey with a night in Delhi, then travel up slowly, seeing the holy river towns on the way.

Either way, we arrange every part. Comfortable cars, a night of rest in between, and plenty of breaks on the mountain roads. We also keep one spare day before the wedding, just in case.

Early December

The most beautiful, quiet time

Early December is a magical time in these mountains. The summer crowds are gone. The sky is clear and blue. Fresh snow sits on the peaks. It is cold, and we will keep everyone warm and comfortable.

Clear blue skies

December days are bright and sunny, with the best mountain views of the year.

Fresh snow on the peaks

The high mountains wear white, a dream backdrop for photos.

Peaceful and quiet

Very few tourists. The temple and valley feel calm and private.

Warm and cosy

Heaters, warm rooms, bonfires, shawls and hot food, everyone stays warm.

Early December, clear skies, and fresh snow on the peaks.

The wedding place

Where the celebration happens

These places have open gardens and space, and can host the wedding for about 50 guests.

Triyuginarayan Maangal Resort

Right next to the temple (250 m). Its own garden for the wedding, plus food, music and decorations. 12 rooms.

Open website ›

Narayan Wedding Resort

About 500 m from the temple. Made for weddings, a lawn with valley views, and a vegetarian kitchen.

Open website ›

Shivalik Valley Resort

About 6 km below, near Sonprayag. A bigger resort with a hall and two garden lawns.

Open website ›

Kedar River Retreat

About 6 km below, beside the river. Calm cottages, lovely for the guests to stay.

Simple food

Fresh, warm vegetarian food is served near the temple.

Care for elders

Short walks, rest stops, and doctors on call. We will take good care of everyone.

Take it slow

The mountains are high but gentle. Rest well and drink water.

We plan the travel

Flights, cars and stays, all arranged for you. Just pack and come.
